title: Delete Characters to Make Fancy String
statement: Call a string *fancy* when it never has the same character three times in a row. Remove as few characters as you can from `s` so that what remains (in its original order) is fancy, and return that remaining string. The result is always unique.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Only runs of equal characters matter. A run of length 1 or 2 is already fine, and a run of length 3 or more must be cut down; keeping exactly two of its characters is both allowed and the least you can delete. So the answer keeps every character except the third, fourth, ... copy inside each run. A brute force could keep deleting one character from any triple it finds, but that rescans the string many times.

## Approach

1. Walk through `s` once, building the answer in the array `result`.
2. For each character `ch`, look at the last two characters already kept.
3. If both exist and both equal `ch`, appending it would make three in a row, so skip it.
4. Otherwise push `ch` onto `result`.
5. Join `result` into the final string.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "leeetcode"`. `l` and the first two `e`s are kept, giving `"lee"`. The third `e` arrives when the last two kept characters are both `e`, so it is skipped. `t`, `c`, `o`, `d` and `e` each differ from the character before them and are kept, so the result is `"leetcode"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each character is examined once with a constant-time check.
- Space: O(n) for the characters kept.

## Pitfalls

- Check `size >= 2` before reading `result[size - 2]`; in Java or C that index would be out of bounds for the first two characters.
- Do not delete the whole run: two copies must stay.
- Building the answer with repeated string concatenation in some languages is O(n²); collect characters and join once.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `result` | characters kept so far, in order |
| `ch` | the current character of `s` |
| `size` | how many characters are kept before `ch` |

narration.2: Collect the kept characters in an array so appending is cheap.
narration.3: Look at every character of s once, from left to right.
narration.4: Note how many characters have been kept so far.
narration.5: If the last two kept characters both equal ch, keeping it would make three in a row.
narration.6: So skip this character; it is one of the extra copies in a long run.
narration.8: Otherwise ch is safe to keep.
narration.10: Join the kept characters into the fancy string.
